questions.question: Needles N1, N2 and N3 are made of a ferromagnetic, a paramagnetic and a diamagnetic substance respectively. A magnet when brought close to them will
options: attract N1 and N2 strongly but repel N3
attract N1 strongly, N2 weakly and repel N3 weakly
attract N1 strongly, but repel N2 and N3 weakly
questions.explanation:
Ferromagnetic substances have strong tendency to get magnetised (induced magnetic moment) in the same direction as that of applied magnetic field, so magnet attracts N1 strongely.
Paramagnetic substances get weakly magnetised (magnetic moment induced is small) in the same direction as that of applied magnetic field, so magnet attract N2 weakly. 
Diamagnetic susbtances also get weakly magnetised when placed in an external magnetic field but in opposite direction and hence N3 is weakly repelled by magnet.

questions.question:
A small bar magnet is moved through a coil at constant speed from one end to the other. Which of the following series of observations will be seen on the galvanometer G attached across the coil ?



Three positions shown describe:
(i) the magnet's entry
(ii) magnet is completely inside and
(iii) magnet's exit
questions.explanation:
At point (i)
The bar magnet enters into the coil, so the magnetic flux passing through the loops will change. In order to oppose that, an emf gets generated and an induced current starts to flow. So, the pointer of galvanometer will deflect in a particular direction.
(We can not be definite about the direction, as which pole of magnet is being entered into the coil is not given.)
At point (ii)
The bar magnet is completely inside the coil, so the flux will not change. No emf will be generated and no current flow. So, the pointer will not deflect towards any side. It will show zero.
At point (iii)
The bar magnet exits from the coil, so again the flux will change in opposite manner to what happened at point (i), so again an opposing emf gets generated and an induced current starts to flow in a direction opposite to that when the magnet was entering.
So in this case, the pointer will deflect in the direction opposite to the case when magnet was entering.
Looking at the options, following cases seems to be possible.



Hence, correct option is (2)

questions.question:
Four different steps that occur during meiosis are given in the following list :-
(i) Complete separation of chromatids by the breakage of centromere
(ii) Pairing of homologous chromosomes
(iii) Alignment of paired chromosomes on equator
(iv) Crossing over between chromatids
Select to correct sequential arrangement of the steps
questions.explanation:
NCERT-XIth, Page. # 126, 127
Explanation
Step (ii) Pairing of homologous chromosomes: This occurs first during prophase I of meiosis, where homologous chromosomes come together to form pairs (synapsis).
Step (iv) Crossing over between chromatids: After pairing, during prophase I, homologous chromosomes exchange segments in a process called crossing over.
Step (iii) Alignment of paired chromosomes on the equator: In metaphase I, the homologous chromosome pairs align along the equator of the cell. Step (i) Complete separation of chromatids by the breakage of the centromere: This occurs in anaphase II (for sister chromatids), where the centromeres break, and the chromatids are separated.
Correct answer: 3. ii, iv, iii, i

questions.question: If A cell have 40 unit DNA, 20 chromosome in prophase I than what should be the amount of DNA and chromosome in gamete respectively :-
questions.explanation:
Answer: 4. 10, 10
Explanation:


\tThe cell in prophase I has 40 units of DNA and 20 chromosomes (diploid state, 2n = 20).
\tAfter meiosis I, the chromosome number is halved (reduction division), and the cells now have 10 chromosomes (haploid, n = 10).
\tDuring meiosis II the DNA is not replicated again, so each gamete will have half the DNA content as the original cell. The DNA will be reduced to 10 units.


Thus, in the gamete, there will be 10 units of DNA and 10 chromosomes.
